question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Insolent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Disrespectful.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Insolent" means showing rude and arrogant disrespect. Its closest synonym among the options is "Disrespectful" (lacking due regard for others). (बदतमीज़, अभद्र)
◦ Example: The insolent (disrespectful) clerk spoke rudely to every customer who asked a question.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Humble" means modest and having a low estimate of one's own importance — the opposite of the arrogance shown by an insolent person.

 

• Option 3 "Courteous" means polite and considerate toward others — the very opposite of the rudeness implied by insolent.

 

• Option 4 "Timid" means lacking courage or confidence — describes shyness, not the bold rudeness of insolence.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of insolent: rude, impertinent, impudent, disrespectful, insulting. Antonyms: polite, courteous, respectful, humble.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Quaint (अनोखा, पुराने ढंग का): Charming (आकर्षक), Old-fashioned (पुराने ढंग का), Picturesque (सुरम्य), Curious (विचित्र)

 

2. Resilient (लचीला, दृढ़): Tough (कठोर), Flexible (लचीला), Hardy (मज़बूत), Adaptable (अनुकूलनीय)

 

3. Skeptical (संशयवादी): Doubtful (संदेहपूर्ण), Dubious (संदिग्ध), Incredulous (अविश्वासी), Distrustful (अविश्वासी)

 

4. Tenacious (दृढ़, हठपूर्वक डटे रहने वाला): Persistent (दृढ़), Determined (दृढ़संकल्प), Steadfast (अटल), Resolute (दृढ़निश्चयी)

 

5. Unwavering (अटल, दृढ़): Steady (स्थिर), Firm (दृढ़), Constant (निरंतर), Resolute (दृढ़निश्चयी)

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

The committee decided to castigate the officer publicly for his negligence in handling the funds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Condemn.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Castigate" means to reprimand or criticize someone severely. Its closest synonym is "Condemn". (कड़ी आलोचना करना, दंड देना)
◦ Correct: The committee decided to castigate (condemn) the officer publicly for his negligence in handling the funds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Praise" (approve), Option 2 "Console" (comfort) and Option 4 "Admire" (respect) are unrelated to the harsh criticism expressed by castigate.

 

NOTE

 

• "Castigate" is most often met in the phrase "castigate someone for" — to harshly criticize a person for a fault. Synonyms: rebuke, reprimand, chastise, condemn, censure. Antonyms: praise, commend, admire, applaud.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Vivacious (जीवंत, उल्लासमय): Lively (जीवंत), Energetic (ऊर्जावान), Animated (सजीव), Spirited (उत्साही)

 

2. Whimsical (सनकी, विचित्र): Fanciful (कल्पनाशील), Capricious (चंचल), Quirky (विलक्षण), Playful (चंचल)

 

3. Xenophobic (विदेशियों से नफरत करने वाला): Prejudiced (पूर्वाग्रही), Intolerant (असहिष्णु), Bigoted (संकीर्णमना), Insular (संकुचित विचारों वाला)

 

4. Yielding (नम्र, झुकने वाला): Compliant (आज्ञाकारी), Submissive (विनीत), Flexible (लचीला), Pliant (नम्य)

 

5. Zealous (उत्साही, जोशीला): Enthusiastic (उत्साही), Passionate (जोशीला), Fervent (उत्कट), Ardent (उत्कट)

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Amiable
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Friendly.

• "Amiable" means friendly and pleasant in nature. Its closest synonym among the options is "Friendly" (warm and good-natured toward others). (मिलनसार, मित्रवत)
◦ Example: Her amiable (friendly) manner put every new visitor at ease within minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

• Option 1 "Hostile" means unfriendly and antagonistic — the direct opposite of the warm nature described by amiable.

 

• Option 2 "Arrogant" means having an exaggerated sense of one's own importance — a proud attitude, not the good-natured warmth of amiable.

 

• Option 3 "Aloof" means cool and distant, not friendly or forthcoming — describes emotional distance, the opposite of amiable's warmth.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of amiable: friendly, genial, affable, good-natured, cordial. Antonyms: hostile, unfriendly, aloof, disagreeable.

3. Dexterous (निपुण, फुर्तीला): Skillful (कुशल), Agile (फुर्तीला), Adept (निपुण), Nimble (चुस्त)

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

The professor's lecture on quantum philosophy was so esoteric that only a handful of specialists could follow it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Mysterious.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Esoteric" means intended for or understood by only a small, specialized group. Its closest synonym is "Mysterious". (गूढ़, केवल कुछ लोगों द्वारा समझा जाने वाला)
◦ Correct: The professor's lecture on quantum philosophy was so esoteric (mysterious) that only a handful of specialists could follow it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 "Popular" (widely known), Option 3 "Obvious" (clear) and Option 4 "Common" (ordinary) are unrelated to the specialized, hard-to-access knowledge described by esoteric.

 

NOTE

 

• "Esoteric" is most often met in the phrase "esoteric knowledge" — knowledge understood by only a select few. Synonyms: abstruse, obscure, arcane, cryptic, recondite. Antonyms: common, popular, well-known, exoteric.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Garrulous (बातूनी): Talkative (बातूनी), Chatty (गपशप करने वाला), Loquacious (वाचाल), Voluble (वाक्पटु)

 

2. Hackneyed (घिसा-पिटा): Cliched (घिसा-पिटा), Trite (पुराना), Overused (अत्यधिक प्रयुक्त), Stale (बासी)

 

3. Immaculate (निर्दोष, बेदाग़): Spotless (बेदाग़), Flawless (निर्दोष), Pristine (अक्षुण्ण), Impeccable (त्रुटिहीन)

 

4. Judicious (विवेकपूर्ण): Sensible (समझदार), Prudent (विवेकपूर्ण), Wise (बुद्धिमान), Sound (ठोस)

 

5. Kindle (प्रज्वलित करना, जगाना): Ignite (जलाना), Arouse (जगाना), Spark (भड़काना), Inflame (भड़काना)

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Ubiquitous
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Omnipresent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Ubiquitous" means present or found everywhere at the same time. Its closest synonym among the options is "Omnipresent" (existing everywhere at once). (सर्वव्यापी, हर जगह मौजूद)
◦ Example: Smartphones have become so ubiquitous (omnipresent) that they appear in nearly every hand on the street.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Rare" means not found or occurring often — the opposite of the widespread presence described by ubiquitous.

 

• Option 3 "Scarce" means insufficient in supply or availability — implies limited quantity, the reverse of being everywhere.

 

• Option 4 "Isolated" means existing apart or separate from others — describes a single, cut-off instance, unlike something found everywhere.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of ubiquitous: omnipresent, universal, pervasive, widespread, everywhere. Antonyms: rare, scarce, uncommon, localized.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Lethargic (सुस्त, आलसी): Sluggish (सुस्त), Listless (निढाल), Torpid (निष्क्रिय), Languid (शिथिल)

 

2. Malleable (लचीला, ढलनशील): Pliable (नम्य), Adaptable (अनुकूलनीय), Flexible (लचीला), Ductile (तन्य)

 

3. Nonchalant (उदासीन, बेपरवाह): Indifferent (उदासीन), Casual (लापरवाह), Unconcerned (निश्चिंत), Blase (निर्विकार)

 

4. Obfuscate (अस्पष्ट करना): Confuse (भ्रमित करना), Obscure (धुंधला करना), Blur (धुंधलाना), Muddle (गड़बड़ाना)

 

5. Placate (शांत करना): Appease (संतुष्ट करना), Pacify (शांत करना), Soothe (सांत्वना देना), Mollify (नरम करना)

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Worsen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Deteriorate" means to become progressively worse. Its closest synonym is "Worsen". (बिगड़ना, अधिक खराब होना)
◦ Correct: The patient's condition began to deteriorate (worsen) rapidly after the infection spread.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Improve" (get better), Option 2 "Stabilize" (stay steady) and Option 4 "Recover" (regain health) are unrelated to the decline in condition described by deteriorate.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of deteriorate: worsen, decline, degenerate, decay, wane. Antonyms: improve, recover, strengthen, ameliorate.

question:

solution_text:

◦ Example: The abstruse (difficult) mathematical proof baffled even the senior researchers.

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Simple" means easy to understand or do — the direct opposite of the complexity implied by abstruse.

 

• Option 2 "Clear" means easily perceived or understood — describes transparency of meaning, the reverse of abstruse.

 

• Option 3 "Evident" means plain or obvious to see or understand — something self-apparent, unlike an abstruse idea that needs effort to grasp.

• Synonyms of abstruse: obscure, esoteric, cryptic, complex, recondite. Antonyms: simple, clear, obvious, evident.

3. Zeal (उत्साह, जोश): Enthusiasm (उत्साह), Passion (जोश), Fervor (उत्कटता), Ardor (उत्साह)

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

The storm began to abate by midnight, allowing rescue teams to resume their search.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Moderate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Abate" means to become less intense or subside. Its closest synonym is "Moderate". (कम होना, शांत होना)
◦ Correct: The storm began to abate (moderate) by midnight, allowing rescue teams to resume their search.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 "Intensify" (grow stronger), Option 3 "Escalate" (increase rapidly) and Option 4 "Amplify" (magnify) are unrelated to the lessening in intensity described by abate.

 

NOTE

 

• "Abate" is most often met in the phrase "the storm/pain abates" — describing something unpleasant that gradually lessens. Synonyms: subside, diminish, wane, ease, moderate. Antonyms: intensify, escalate, increase, amplify.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Candor (स्पष्टवादिता): Honesty (ईमानदारी), Frankness (स्पष्टता), Openness (खुलापन), Sincerity (निष्कपटता)

 

2. Debacle (पूर्ण विफलता, तबाही): Fiasco (असफलता), Disaster (आपदा), Collapse (पतन), Failure (विफलता)

 

3. Effervescent (उत्साही, जोशीला): Bubbly (उमंगी), Vivacious (जीवंत), Ebullient (उत्साही), Sparkling (चमकीला)

 

4. Frivolous (तुच्छ, हल्का): Trivial (तुच्छ), Silly (मूर्खतापूर्ण), Petty (छोटा), Superficial (सतही)

 

5. Grandiose (भव्य, दिखावटी): Grand (भव्य), Pompous (आडंबरपूर्ण), Extravagant (अतिशय), Ostentatious (दिखावटी)

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Loathe
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Hate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Loathe" means to feel intense dislike or disgust for. Its closest synonym among the options is "Hate" (to feel intense dislike for). (घृणा करना, नफरत करना)
◦ Example: She loathed (hated) having to wake up early on cold winter mornings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Admire" means to regard with respect and warm approval — it expresses a positive feeling, the opposite of the strong aversion in loathe.

 

• Option 3 "Cherish" means to hold something dear and treat it with tender care — it conveys fondness, not the intense dislike of loathe.

 

• Option 4 "Adore" means to love or admire someone/something deeply — it is a term of great affection, the reverse of loathe.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of loathe: detest, abhor, despise, hate, abominate. Antonyms: adore, admire, love, cherish.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Frugal (मितव्ययी): Thrifty (मितव्ययी), Economical (किफायती), Sparing (कम खर्चीला), Parsimonious (कंजूस)

 

2. Meticulous (बहुत सावधान, बारीकी से ध्यान देने वाला): Careful (सावधान), Precise (सटीक), Thorough (गहन), Painstaking (परिश्रमी)

 

3. Candid (स्पष्टवादी, निष्कपट): Frank (स्पष्टवादी), Honest (ईमानदार), Sincere (निष्कपट), Forthright (स्पष्ट)

 

4. Obsolete (अप्रचलित, पुराना): Outdated (पुराना), Archaic (प्राचीन), Antiquated (दकियानूसी), Outmoded (चलन से बाहर)

 

5. Tenacious (दृढ़, हठपूर्वक डटे रहने वाला): Persistent (दृढ़), Persevering (लगनशील), Steadfast (अडिग), Determined (दृढ़ निश्चयी)

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

The scientists were faced with a conundrum that none of their existing theories could explain.

◦ Correct: The scientists were faced with a conundrum (problem) that none of their existing theories could explain.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Solution" (an answer to a problem), Option 2 "Answer" (a reply or resolution) and Option 4 "Certainty" (something sure or definite) are unrelated to the sense of an unresolved, puzzling difficulty that conundrum conveys.

2. Austere (कठोर, सादा): Stern (कठोर), Strict (सख्त), Severe (कड़ा), Ascetic (तपस्वी)

 

3. Pragmatic (व्यावहारिक): Practical (व्यावहारिक), Realistic (यथार्थवादी), Sensible (समझदार), Down-to-earth (सीधा-सादा)

 

4. Zealous (उत्साही, जोशीला): Enthusiastic (उत्साही), Passionate (जोशीला), Fervent (उत्कट), Ardent (प्रबल)

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Defer
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Delay.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Defer" means to put off an action or event to a later time. Its closest synonym among the options is "Delay" (to put off to a later time). (स्थगित करना, रोकना)
◦ Example: The committee decided to defer (delay) the meeting until all members could attend.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Advance" means to move something forward in time or position — it is nearly opposite to defer, which means to push something back.

 

• Option 2 "Expedite" means to make a process happen faster — it speeds things up, the reverse of deferring, which delays them.

 

• Option 3 "Cancel" means to call off an event entirely — it ends the matter completely, unlike defer, which only delays it to a later time.

 

NOTE

 

• "Defer" is most often met in the phrase "defer to" — meaning to yield to someone's judgment or authority out of respect. Synonyms: postpone, delay, adjourn, shelve, suspend. Antonyms: advance, expedite, hasten, accelerate.

 

5 Important Synonyms

 

1. Vindictive (प्रतिशोधी): Vengeful (प्रतिशोधी), Spiteful (द्वेषपूर्ण), Revengeful (बदला लेने वाला), Resentful (रोषयुक्त)

 

2. Prudent (विवेकपूर्ण, समझदार): Wise (बुद्धिमान), Sensible (समझदार), Judicious (विवेकपूर्ण), Cautious (सतर्क)

 

3. Gregarious (मिलनसार, सामाजिक): Sociable (मिलनसार), Outgoing (खुले स्वभाव का), Convivial (मेलजोल वाला), Companionable (साथी स्वभाव का)

 

4. Obstinate (जिद्दी): Stubborn (जिद्दी), Headstrong (हठी), Inflexible (अटल), Unyielding (न झुकने वाला)

 

5. Servile (दास जैसा, चापलूस): Submissive (दब्बू), Obsequious (चापलूस), Subservient (अधीनस्थ), Slavish (गुलामी भरा)

question:

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 "Mature" (fully developed), Option 3 "Adult" (a grown person) and Option 4 "Elderly" (old in age) are unrelated to the childish, immature quality that juvenile conveys.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of juvenile: childish, immature, youthful, puerile, adolescent. Antonyms: mature, adult, grown-up, sensible.

Bawdy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Coarse.

• "Bawdy" means humorously vulgar or indecent, especially about sexual matters. Its closest synonym among the options is "Coarse" (crude and lacking refinement). (अश्लील, भद्दा)
◦ Example: The comedian's bawdy (coarse) jokes made some members of the audience uncomfortable.

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Refined" means elegant and cultured in manner — it is the opposite of bawdy, which is crude and indecent.

 

• Option 2 "Polite" means showing good manners and courtesy — it describes respectable behavior, unlike the vulgar tone of bawdy.

 

• Option 3 "Modest" means decent and free from vanity or indecency — it stands in direct contrast to the indecent humor of bawdy.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of bawdy: coarse, vulgar, lewd, ribald, indecent. Antonyms: refined, modest, polite, decent.

• Option 4 "Vigorous" means full of physical strength and energy — it directly contrasts with the weakness described by feeble.

question:

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Pacify.

• "Allay" means to diminish or calm fear, worry, or suspicion. Its closest synonym is "Pacify". (शांत करना, डर/चिंता कम करना)
◦ Correct: The manager tried to allay (pacify) the employees' fears about upcoming layoffs by holding an open meeting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Provoke" (to stir up a strong reaction), Option 2 "Intensify" (to make stronger or more severe) and Option 4 "Aggravate" (to make a problem worse) are unrelated to the calming, fear-reducing sense that allay conveys.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of allay: pacify, calm, soothe, alleviate, ease. Antonyms: provoke, aggravate, intensify, incite.
